paragraphs.text: Jeffrey "Jeff" Gomez , also credited as Jeffrey Goméz-Artemis , was the editor and main author of several Armada Magic: The Gathering comics in 1995 - 1996 . Since 2000, he has been the CEO of Starlight Runner Entertainment , a leading producer of highly successful fictional "Worlds," which maximize the value of intellectual properties by preparing them for licensing, merchandising, and extension across multiple media platforms. He is considered to be an expert in the fields of brand narrative, story world development, creative franchise design, and transmedia storytelling.

An avid gamer, Jeff started his career in gaming journalism at Gateways magazine - covering adventure games, role-playing games such as Dungeons & Dragons, early computer games and genre books, television and films from a cross-platform "universe" perspective - before moving to Valiant Comics in 1992. After he learned that the video game company Acclaim Entertainment (makers of the Mortal Kombat series) intended to buy Valiant in the hopes of adapting their superheroes into games, he volunteered to help select and develop the games from the Valiant side. His pick for the first big Nintendo 64 game was Turok, Dinosaur Hunter , and he submitted a concept document that led to him being a producer on the game. The game was considered a huge success.

For his next project, Gomez recommended a trading card game being made by some friends of his from his days as a tabletop game writer: Magic: The Gathering . When he received the go-ahead to reach out to Wizards of the Coast , he learned that there was fierce competition for the Magic license from all the comic book companies, including Marvel and DC . What made Acclaim stand out was that they also wanted the game license, and that Gomez had a lot of experience helping to build expansive fantasy worlds.

Once Wizards of the Coast approved, Valiant turned to Gomez to lead the project on short notice. Finding a writer to create the ARMADA imprint comics and games ( Magic: The Gathering - BattleMage , Magic: The Gathering - Armageddon and Rise of the Mana Wraith ) so quickly was nearly impossible, so he proposed to write for them himself. As they gave him less than a month to have the first script in production as a comic, he took a shortcut. He went to one of his original Dungeons & Dragons campaign settings, The Land of Corondor , and plopped it down in the middle of Dominaria . That way, he could wreck the place and have some creative freedom without messing with the rest of the Magic multiverse too badly. Not much later, Wizards gave him the freedom to expand, like telling the origin story of Dakkon Blackblade and set it on Corondor and the origin story for the whole Carthalion family saga that tied together the comics and video games. They also let him tell stories set elsewhere on Dominaria during the Ice Age era , allowing him to tie his various comic book series together in the form of a grand epic that took place over the course of many centuries. Running just short of Planeswalker War before cancellation of the comics line was one of the most crushing disappointments of his career. His favorite character was Jared Carthalion , who has a scar on his face just like him.

After leaving the comics and video game industry in the late 1990s, Jeff co-founded Starlight Runner Entertainment in 2000 with Mark Pensavalle and Chrysoula Artemis. As a producer accredited by the Producers Guild of America, Jeff also develops the story worlds of films, TV shows, videogames, toys, books, comics, apps, virtual reality projects, and theme park attractions. Jeff’s pop culture work has impacted such blockbuster properties as Disney’s Pirates of the Caribbean , James Cameron’s Avatar , Hasbro ’s Transformers , Sony Pictures’ Spider-Man and Men in Black , Microsoft’s Halo , and Nickelodeon’s Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles .
